summary: Blends, sequences, or constrains camera/object transforms and camera viewing settings from multiple input Camera COMPs, letting a build animate between camera rigs without hand-copying transform channels.

key_params.name: parenttype
key_params.note: Blend, Sequence, or Constrain method for combining input parent transforms

key_params.name: sequence
key_params.note: Selects the active input when using Sequence or Constrain mode

key_params.name: reset
key_params.note: Frame at which constrain mode resets its relative transform

key_params.name: blendw1
key_params.note: Weight for the first input in Blend mode

key_params.name: blendm1
key_params.note: Components of the first input transform used during blending

key_params.name: blendw2
key_params.note: Weight for the second input in Blend mode

key_params.name: blendm2
key_params.note: Components of the second input transform used during blending

key_concepts: Camera Blend COMP blends object transforms and camera viewing settings from multiple Camera COMPs into one camera output.
Camera inputs are wired from Camera COMP bottom connectors into the Camera Blend COMP top inputs.
Blend mode combines up to the first four inputs using matching weight and mask parameters.
Sequence and Constrain modes select an input parent over time, with Constrain preserving relative transform until the reset frame.
When non-Camera COMPs are connected, the Camera Blend COMP uses its own View and Background pages for camera settings.
common_gotchas: Inputs come from the bottom connector of Camera COMPs into the Camera Blend COMP top inputs.
Blend mode only uses up to the first four inputs with the corresponding weight and mask parameters.
When non-Camera COMPs are connected, the Camera Blend COMP uses its own View and Background parameter pages for camera settings.
In Sequence mode, values outside the input range can behave like unparenting the child.
Constrain mode maintains relative transform as the parent changes and depends on the reset frame for predictable reset behavior.
Short rotation only applies to two-input quaternion blending cases.
